\section[la burocrazia]{la burocrazia — the bureaucracy, the red tape}

\label{lesson:IT-C389-burocrazia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the renewal, then the Italian for the card.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la burocrazia}
\textbf{la burocrazia} — \textquotedblleft{}the bureaucracy, the red tape\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Per aprire un negozio c'è troppa burocrazia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{To open a shop there is too much red tape.}
\end{quote}

Stress on \emph{-zìa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{burocrazia} was borrowed from French \emph{bureaucratie}, built from \emph{bureau} \textquotedblleft{}desk, office\textquotedblright{} and \emph{-cratie} \textquotedblleft{}rule of\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), a Greek ending, from \emph{krátos} \textquotedblleft{}power\textquotedblright{}: rule by the desk.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la burocrazia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la burocrazia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the renewal, then the Italian for the card, then say \emph{la burocrazia} again

\section[la pratica]{la pratica — the paperwork, the case (being handled); the practice}

\label{lesson:IT-C389-pratica}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the card, then the Italian for the bureaucracy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la pratica}
\textbf{la pratica} — \textquotedblleft{}the paperwork, the case (being handled); the practice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La mia pratica è ancora in comune.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My paperwork is still at the town hall.}
\end{quote}

\emph{In pratica} — in practice, basically. \emph{Fare pratica} — to get experience.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pratica} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{practica}, related to \emph{practicus} \textquotedblleft{}active\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from Greek \emph{praktik\'{\={e}}} \textquotedblleft{}practical knowledge\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{prássein} \textquotedblleft{}to do, to act\textquotedblright{}; the office sense is a matter being dealt with.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la procedura]{la procedura — the procedure}

\label{lesson:IT-C389-procedura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the bureaucracy, then the Italian for the paperwork.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la procedura}
\textbf{la procedura} — \textquotedblleft{}the procedure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La procedura è lunga, ma non è difficile.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The procedure is long, but it is not difficult.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Seguire la procedura} — to follow the procedure.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{procedura} came from French \emph{procédure}, built on \emph{procéder}, from Latin \emph{prōcēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to go forward\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{cēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la richiesta]{la richiesta — the request, the application}

\label{lesson:IT-C389-richiesta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the paperwork, then the Italian for the procedure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la richiesta}
\textbf{la richiesta} — \textquotedblleft{}the request, the application\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho fatto richiesta di un nuovo documento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have applied for a new document.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Su richiesta} — on request. \emph{Fare richiesta di} — to apply for.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{richiesta} is built on \emph{richiedere} \textquotedblleft{}to request\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{ri-} and \emph{chiedere} \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{quaerere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek, to ask\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il certificato]{il certificato — the certificate}

\label{lesson:IT-C389-certificato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the procedure, then the Italian for the request.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il certificato}
\textbf{il certificato} — \textquotedblleft{}the certificate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se sei malato, devi portare un certificato medico.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you are ill, you have to bring a medical certificate.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Il certificato di nascita} — the birth certificate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{certificato} is built on \emph{certificare} \textquotedblleft{}to certify\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{certificāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make certain\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{certus} \textquotedblleft{}sure\textquotedblright{} and \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
